comparison: Both evaluate claims about the open conformation (C5, C34-C40, C78-C81). OpenEval finds the structural data supporting the open conformation claim, noting low crystal contact areas argue against crystallization artifacts. Peer review challenges the interpretation, stating 'several different structures does not mean the protein is inherently more flexible' and questions which ligands trigger open vs closed states. Structural observations accepted but functional interpretation disputed.

Both evaluate disulfide bridge experiments (C41-C45). OpenEval finds strong support from Ellman reaction and functional assays showing selective helicase impairment. Peer review explicitly praises this approach as 'particularly clever' for testing the closed form. Complete agreement on experimental design and conclusions.

Both evaluate ATPase characterization (C46-C49). OpenEval finds the systematic measurements and species comparison well-supported. Peer review accepts the core biochemical data as 'very high quality' but requests additional controls in Table 3 and questions one specific result about hook-loop mutants. General agreement with minor requests for completeness.

Both evaluate background/literature claims (C1-C2, C8-C22). OpenEval notes these are appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer review does not dispute factual content but criticizes incomplete contextualization, stating authors 'appeared to be functioning in a bubble, seemingly unaware of the vast crystallographic and biochemical literature.' Agreement on cited facts, disagreement on comprehensiveness.

Both evaluate the ratcheting mechanism claim (C87). OpenEval acknowledges this is a negative result based on structural interpretation and notes alternative mechanisms cannot be ruled out. Peer review directly questions the evidence: 'what is the evidence that this domain is ratcheting? If they have no evidence, they should consider a more cautious nomenclature.' Both recognize limitations but peer review more critical of nomenclature.

Both evaluate RNA binding and structural observations (C4, C24-C33 in OpenEval; adds C3, C23 in peer review). OpenEval finds crystallographic data well-supporting sequence-independent RNA binding with minimal base-specific interactions. Peer review challenges novelty, stating 'RNA binding tunnel of Prp43 is essentially the same as previously reported for MLE' and notes 'RNA seems to be less well defined in the electron density.' Structural data not disputed but novelty and significance questioned.

Both evaluate conserved RNA interaction patterns (C72-C77 in OpenEval; adds C67-C71 in peer review). OpenEval finds strong support from structural comparisons showing spatially conserved interactions despite sequence divergence. Peer review notes 'RNA binding tunnel of Prp43 is essentially the same as previously reported for MLE' and requests comparison with NS3 work, indicating inadequate contextualization. Agreement on structural observations but disagreement on novelty and proper comparison to literature.

Both evaluate Hook-Turn mutant functional data (C53-C56, C60-C65 in OpenEval; adds C6, C50-C52, C57-C59, C66, C83-C86 in peer review). OpenEval finds multiple complementary assays well-supporting selective loss of unwinding function. Peer review identifies critical missing control: 'biochemical evidence that the proposed Prp43 hook-loop binds RNA' and questions whether impaired unwinding reflects failed translocation or simply failed substrate binding. Agreement on data quality but disagreement on interpretation and completeness of controls.

Both evaluate Hook-Loop dispensability and mechanistic differences from MLE (C7, C55-C56, C83-C86, C88 in OpenEval; C7, C55, C88 in peer review). OpenEval finds strong support from functional, structural, and evolutionary evidence for distinct mechanism. Peer review finds the mechanistic difference 'interesting' but criticizes authors for 'playing down previous work' with 'inappropriate first claims' and 'misrepresenting novelty.' Mechanistic difference not disputed but contextualization and novelty claims heavily criticized.

OpenEval evaluates ATP-induced conformational changes (C6, C50-C52, C57, C82) finding support from structural comparisons between nucleotide states. Peer review R8 specifically addresses C82 (structural similarity to MLE in ATP-analog state) without specific challenge. Partial overlap with OpenEval finding support and peer review not disputing this particular structural comparison.

Both evaluate sequence-independent RNA binding rationale (C67-C70 in OpenEval; adds C71-C77 in peer review). OpenEval finds the logic connecting minimal base interactions to functional requirements well-reasoned though not directly demonstrated. Peer review questions novelty, noting the RNA binding tunnel is 'essentially the same as previously reported for MLE' and requests better comparison with other helicases. Agreement on structural observations but disagreement on novelty and contextualization.

OpenEval evaluates crystallographic quality (C3, C23, C34) finding strong experimental support with appropriate resolution and refinement statistics. Peer review R1 includes C3, C23 among evaluated claims but focuses criticism on novelty and RNA electron density quality rather than crystallographic methods. Partial overlap with OpenEval accepting technical quality while peer review questions biological significance.

OpenEval evaluates speculative mechanistic claim C66 about Hook-Turn mutants lacking RNA-stimulated ATPase, rating it UNCERTAIN and requesting additional experiments. Peer review R4 includes C66 among evaluated claims and similarly identifies missing controls for RNA binding measurements. Both recognize the need for additional validation of mechanistic interpretations.

OpenEval evaluates Hook-Turn flexibility observations (C58-C59) finding support from crystallographic data showing alternative conformations, though functional significance is not established. Peer review R4 includes these claims but does not specifically address the flexibility observations, focusing instead on missing RNA binding controls for the mutants. Limited overlap in evaluation focus.

OpenEval evaluates comparison between MLE and Prp43 RNA-binding specificity (C71) finding clear support from structural data. Peer review R6 includes C71 and notes 'RNA binding tunnel of Prp43 is essentially the same as previously reported for MLE,' questioning the novelty of the comparison. Agreement on structural differences but disagreement on significance and novelty.
